clue.text: Film assured, but novel flawed

indicators.note: something flawed is faulty or out of shape, so the letters before it are put into a new order

parts.note: fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A reviewer finds a film confident in tone but the novel it was adapted from disappointing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunset Boulevard is Billy Wilder's 1950 Hollywood movie starring Gloria Swanson, so it is an example of a film.

clue.text: Jam shelves next to cash register

parts.note: display stands are shelving units
a till is the drawer or machine holding a shop's cash

explanation.surface: A shopper is stuck in a crowded aisle between the shelving and the checkout.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic jam brings everything to a halt, which is a standstill.

clue.text: Myopic Spooner's prophet given KBE

indicators.note: Dr Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of two words are exchanged

parts.note: a seer is a prophet; its first sound swaps with the next word's
a KBE is a knighthood, so its holder has been knighted; its first sound swaps with the previous word's

explanation.surface: A prophet honoured with a knighthood turns out to be short-sighted, which is ironic for a visionary.
explanation.walkthrough: KBE is Knight Commander of the Order of the British Empire, a British honour; the silent K of the second word makes the swap work by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopia is the medical name for being unable to see distant things clearly, the condition of a near-sighted person.

clue.text: About to avoid coyote, the wild canine

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder and running amok, so the remaining letters are scrambled
to avoid something is to leave it out, so a letter is taken away from the words that follow

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning to keep clear of a coyote, described as the wild dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canine' looks like the noun for a dog, matching coyote, but here it is the tooth. C leaves the coyote, and the eight letters left are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye tooth is the pointed tooth below the eye in the upper jaw, also called a canine tooth.

clue.text: Pause as swimmer checks Rhine's banks

indicators.note: to check something is to hold it back or restrain it, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a bather is someone swimming

indicators.note: the banks of a river are its two edges, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Rhine

explanation.surface: A swimmer in the Rhine stops for a rest to check the riverbanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A breather is a short break taken to recover one's breath, so it is a pause.

clue.text: Disregarded 27 turning up to grab tabloid

indicators.note: to grab something is to take hold of it, so one piece clasps the other
in a down clue, turning up means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: the answer to 27 Down
The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: An overlooked animal appears in the news when a tabloid picks up the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is the answer to 27 Down, an African antelope. The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsung heroes are those whose deeds go unpraised and unnoticed, so the word means disregarded.

clue.text: Weak, needing energy following gala

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a fete is a festive gala or fair

explanation.surface: Someone feeling drained needs a boost of energy after a long day at the gala.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' looks like it is placing energy after gala, but it supplies its own letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete describes someone feeble, lacking vigour or character, which is a synonym of weak.

clue.text: Echo in American gym

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
PE, physical education, is school gym class

explanation.surface: A sound echoes around an American gymnasium.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to copy or mimic them, just as to echo can mean to repeat what another says.

clue.text: Points raised in custody

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are lifted to read from bottom to top
in tells us the letters are sitting inside the next word

parts.note: the inner letters of custody

explanation.surface: Points are raised about someone held in police custody.
explanation.definitionFit: Dots are small points, such as the full stops or the points on a dice face.

clue.text: Understanding of war seen as lost

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grasps that a war is now seen as a lost cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Awareness is knowledge or perception of a situation, a synonym of understanding.

clue.text: Flying squadron may be part of this larger group

definitions.meaning: first meaning: swift, moving very fast

definitions.text: squadron may be part of this larger group
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a naval force made up of several squadrons of ships

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying squadron' reads as one naval or police unit, but the clue splits it: the first word is one meaning, the rest describes the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet as an adjective means quick or nimble, and as a noun names a navy's body of ships, which can contain squadrons.

clue.text: Hand round good-looking person not allowed!

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
out means ruled out or not permitted

explanation.surface: An exclamation forbidding an attractive person from passing something around.
explanation.definitionFit: To dish out food or advice is to distribute it, handing it round to others.

clue.text: Margaret is after fruitcake spice

indicators.note: is after tells us the first named piece comes later in the answer than the second

parts.note: a nut, like a fruitcake, is slang for a crazy person
Meg is a short form of Margaret

explanation.surface: Margaret is looking for the spice needed to make a fruitcake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruitcake' sits in a baking scene, but here it means an eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmeg is the aromatic seed of a tropical tree, ground and used as a kitchen spice.

clue.text: Go onto stage, terribly irate about northern comedian maybe

parts.note: to enter is to come on stage in a script

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another
terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A comic from the north walks on stage furious.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian is one kind of entertainer, someone who amuses an audience; 'maybe' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Mischievous people spark stern reforms

indicators.note: to reform is to form again in a new shape, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Troublemakers prompt strict changes to the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Pranksters are people who play practical jokes, a mischievous sort.

clue.text: Incognito, get heroin, not completely stable

indicators.note: not completely means only part of the run of words is used, the letters sitting inside them

parts.note: the end of incognito, all of get and the start of heroin

explanation.surface: Someone in disguise buys heroin while far from stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not completely stable' reads as one phrase about an unsteady person, but 'not completely' is the hidden signal and 'stable' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A together person is composed and emotionally balanced, an informal sense matching stable.

clue.text: Son cheers Republican VIP

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
ta is British slang for thanks
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A son applauds an important Republican politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheers' looks like applause, but in British usage both cheers and ta mean thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a celebrity, a very important person who draws attention.

clue.text: Drink and simple trimmed steak

parts.note: green means naive or inexperienced

indicators.note: trimming cuts off the edges, so only the inner letters of the word survive

parts.note: steak with its first and last letters cut off

explanation.surface: A meal order: a drink and a plain steak with the fat cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'simple' sounds like plain food, but here it means unworldly.
explanation.definitionFit: Green tea is a beverage made from unfermented tea leaves, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Strolled with deer and relaxed

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with

indicators.note: relaxed means loosened, so the letters are set free to fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone ambled through a park among the deer, feeling at ease.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander is to walk aimlessly or at leisure, so wandered is a synonym of strolled.

clue.text: A time to leave coffee behind

indicators.note: to leave means to go away, so a letter departs from the word that follows

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee
T is the abbreviation for time; 'A' asks for one of them

explanation.surface: Someone notes it's time to go and abandon their coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like it means left behind, but it is the definition: one of the two Ts leaves the coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Being behind schedule means running late, so late is a synonym for behind.

clue.text: Versatile lunar trio docked for preliminary test

indicators.note: versatile means able to turn to many things, so the letters can be turned into a new order
a docked tail is cut short, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Three astronauts docked their spacecraft to rehearse a mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' belongs to the space scene, but it cuts the final O from trio before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run is a rehearsal or test carried out before the real thing, so it is a preliminary test.

clue.text: Remarkable green light?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an indication to go, such as a traffic light

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like admiring an unusual green light; the adjective sense, as in 'a signal achievement', is the less familiar one.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal as an adjective means striking or conspicuous, and as a noun means a sign giving an instruction, like a go-ahead light.

clue.text: Picked up judges for theatrical shows

indicators.note: picked up suggests something caught by the ear, so we want a word that sounds like another

parts.note: to review a performance is to judge it

explanation.surface: Critics are collected to assess stage productions.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a light theatrical entertainment of sketches, songs and dances.

clue.text: Applaud promo introducing Slough

indicators.note: introducing means bringing on first, so one piece goes ahead of the other

parts.note: an ad, a promotional advertisement
a slough is a swamp or bog, as is a mire

explanation.surface: Praise for an advertising campaign promoting the English town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, famously mocked; the capital letter hides the common noun for a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: To applaud someone is to praise or show approval, as when we admire them.

clue.text: Aims to curb habit, being upright?

indicators.note: to curb is to restrain or hem in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: ends are goals or aims
a way is a habitual manner of behaving

explanation.surface: Someone tries to break a bad habit by being a model of good behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upright' looks moral, but here it is literal: standing on end.
explanation.definitionFit: Endways means standing on end, vertical rather than lying flat, so upright in posture.

clue.text: In Lincoln, perhaps daughter's not up yet

parts.note: Abe, as in President Abraham Lincoln, is an example of the name
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Visiting the city of Lincoln, a parent notes their daughter is still asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln suggests the English city, but it is Honest Abe, the US president.
explanation.definitionFit: Abed means in bed, so someone abed has not yet got up.

clue.text: Open beer occasionally, and another drink

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first and third letters of beer
gin is a spirit, a different drink from beer

explanation.surface: Crack open a beer now and then, and have a gin too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' looks like an instruction to open a bottle, but it is the verb meaning to start.
explanation.definitionFit: To open a meeting or a show is to begin it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: African resident gens up on striking ESP

indicators.note: striking means crossing out, so certain letters are struck from the words before

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letters to be struck out

explanation.surface: A local in Africa reads up on extrasensory perception.
explanation.walkthrough: To gen up is British slang for finding out about something. Strike E, S and P from the first two words and three letters remain.
explanation.definitionFit: The gnu, or wildebeest, is an antelope native to Africa, so it lives there.

clue.text: Declaration of perfect Bolero, say — Dean initially wiped out

parts.note: utter means complete or absolute, as in an utter delight

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word just before it, the letter to be removed
wiped out means erased, so that letter disappears

parts.note: the bolero is a Spanish dance
the first letter of Dean

explanation.surface: Praise for the perfect Bolero performance by skaters Torvill and Dean, with Dean wiping out on the ice.
explanation.walkthrough: Torvill and Dean won Olympic ice-dance gold in 1984 skating to Ravel's Bolero, which makes 'Dean' look like part of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: An utterance is something said aloud, a statement, so it can be a declaration.

clue.text: Rules unfairly applied in tennis match and darts, unfortunately

parts.note: a doubles is a tennis match between pairs

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that a tennis match and a darts game are refereed unevenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Double standards are principles applied more strictly to some people than to others, so rules unfairly enforced.
